checks: actual offline CLI and production dependencies

findingsDuringImplementation: Review found that a killed maintenance job could leave scratch directories incompatible with routine worker cleanup. Both now use the existing run-<32 hex> convention and shared ownership-scoped cleanup; SIGKILL/retry checks assert scratch removal.
Allowing maintenance history at initialization must not allow a missing store to be replaced with a new identity. Explicit missing-store refusal and a focused control cover this.
The initial image invocation supplied a timestamp where APP_BUILD_DATE requires YYYY-MM-DD. It failed before app compilation; the corrected invocation used the identical signed source and passed.
limits: There is no older deployed public schema and no fabricated schema transition. The first actual transition must ship an explicit source/target migration and crash/retry tests in its target image.
Maintenance success remains fenced until an unchanged-state resume or a future reviewed migration completion. No generic SQL, force-open, restore promotion or private intermediate upgrader was added.
Backup decryption identity is used only in offline preparation, not in API/worker configuration. Fixture identities were generated and discarded; real custody remains an activation check.

Protected copies are excluded from routine retention. Expiry is an explicit offline operator command, after resolution/seven days and verification of a post-resolution routine backup. Failures may extend retention.

B2 transfers used a controlled protocol destination. The production-image CLI rehearsal had no external network and only tmpfs state; no actual bucket, public deployment, registry push or Tailscale data was used.
Process-crash tests are not a host power-loss durability proof; cleanup is not forensic erasure.
Release qualification and the personal history-management walkthrough remain paused.
